question_text: Find the angle between the following line segments and the base plane of the triangular prism:

mark_breakdown.desc: Identify projection [DE] and setup trigonometric ratio for angle AED

subparts.solution:
The projection of $[\text{AE}]$ onto the base plane is $[\text{DE}]$.
$\therefore$ the required angle is $\text{A}\hat{\text{E}}\text{D}$.
$$\tan\theta = \frac{4}{10}$$
$$\therefore \theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{10}\right) \approx 21.8^{\circ}$$
The angle is about $21.8^{\circ}$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The angle between a line and a plane is the angle between the line and its orthogonal projection on that plane.
step_by_step: Project vertex A vertically down onto the base plane, which gives point D.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Confusing the hypotenuse with the base side, or projecting onto the wrong edge of the base.

mark_breakdown.desc: Identify projection [CD] and state tan ratio for angle BDC
Compute inverse tangent to find angle approximately 20.0°

subparts.solution:
The projection of $[\text{BD}]$ onto the base plane is $[\text{CD}]$.
$\therefore$ the required angle is $\text{B}\hat{\text{D}}\text{C}$.
$$\tan\theta = \frac{4}{11}$$
$$\therefore \theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{11}\right) \approx 20.0^{\circ}$$
The angle is about $20.0^{\circ}$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The angle between a line and a plane is formed by the line and its projection onto the plane.
step_by_step: The orthogonal projection of B onto the base plane is C, so the projection of $[\text{BD}]$ is $[\text{CD}]$.
In right-angled triangle $\Delta \text{BCD}$, the opposite side is $\text{BC} = 4\text{ cm}$ and the adjacent side is $\text{CD} = 11\text{ cm}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Incorrectly identifying the adjacent side length along the base plane.

mark_breakdown.desc: Use Pythagoras' theorem in triangle ECF to find length of base diagonal CE
Formulate tan ratio for angle BEC

subparts.solution:
The projection of $[\text{BE}]$ onto the base plane is $[\text{CE}]$.
$\therefore$ the required angle is $\text{B}\hat{\text{E}}\text{C}$.
Let $\text{CE}$ be $x\text{ cm}$.
Using Pythagoras in $\Delta \text{ECF}$:
$$x^2 = 10^2 + 11^2 = 221$$
$$\therefore x = \sqrt{221} \quad \{x > 0\}$$
Let $\text{B}\hat{\text{E}}\text{C}$ be $\alpha$.
$$\therefore \tan\alpha = \frac{4}{\sqrt{221}}$$
$$\therefore \alpha = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{\sqrt{221}}\right) \approx 15.1^{\circ}$$
The angle is about $15.1^{\circ}$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: In 3D trigonometry, the projection of a space diagonal onto a base plane requires calculating the 2D plane diagonal first via Pythagoras' theorem.
step_by_step: Find the length of projection $[\text{CE}]$ in the rectangular base: $\text{CE} = \sqrt{10^2 + 11^2} = \sqrt{221}$.
In the vertical right triangle $\Delta \text{BCE}$, side $\text{BC} = 4$ is perpendicular to the base plane.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Premature rounding of the intermediate length $\sqrt{221}$, leading to inaccuracies.

mark_breakdown.desc: Use Pythagoras' theorem to calculate base segment DM
Set up tan ratio for angle AMD

subparts.solution:
The projection of $[\text{AM}]$ onto the base plane is $[\text{DM}]$.
$\therefore$ the required angle is $\text{A}\hat{\text{M}}\text{D}$.
Let $\text{DM}$ be $x\text{ cm}$.
Using Pythagoras in $\Delta \text{DCM}$:
$$x^2 = 11^2 + 5^2 = 146$$
$$\therefore x = \sqrt{146} \quad \{x > 0\}$$
Let $\text{A}\hat{\text{M}}\text{D}$ be $\alpha$.
$$\therefore \tan\alpha = \frac{4}{\sqrt{146}}$$
$$\therefore \alpha = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{\sqrt{146}}\right) \approx 18.3^{\circ}$$
The angle is about $18.3^{\circ}$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Find the length of the projection segment on the base using the coordinates or right-triangle geometry of the base, then apply the tangent ratio with the vertical height.
step_by_step: M is the midpoint of the side of length 10 cm, so $\text{CM} = 5\text{ cm}$.
Find $\text{DM}$ using the right triangle $\Delta \text{DCM}$: $\text{DM} = \sqrt{11^2 + 5^2} = \sqrt{146}\text{ cm}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using the full length of 10 cm instead of the half-length 5 cm to the midpoint M.
